notes: The schematic is treated as the authority for connectivity: LMV358 section 1 is a non-inverting amplifier. IN1+ is biased by R8 (100k to IOREF/3.3V) and R9 (100k to GND) and fed from the jack through C1 (100nF). IN1- goes to GND through R10 (47k) and to the trimmer through R11 (47k). The trimmer wiper goes to OUT1, and OUT1 goes to A0. Gain = 1 + trimmer/R11 ratio as the schematic shows.
The Arduino Zero is not in the catalogue and is created as a new type. Its IOREF pin supplies the 3.3 V reference, as drawn in the schematic and the Fritzing image.

The exact breadboard holes are my approximation of the Fritzing image. I kept the schematic connectivity and placed the parts in 't' (rows a-e) and 'b' (rows f-j) banks accordingly. In particular, the trimmer pins are placed in the 't' bank and the purple wire goes from its wiper column to the op-amp output column. Rail hole numbers are approximate.

LMV358 pins: 1 OUT1, 2 IN1-, 3 IN1+, 4 GND, 5 IN2+, 6 IN2-, 7 OUT2, 8 VCC. The chip straddles the centre gap with pins 1-4 in columns 14-17 of the 't' bank and pins 8-5 in columns 14-17 of the 'b' bank. The second amplifier section is unused; its pins are joined to the breadboard but nothing is connected on them, so no electrical edges are added for pins 5-7.
The trimmer's third lug (VCC) is left unconnected, as shown in the schematic (red unconnected end). The jack's LEFT lug is unused.
The jack's sleeve goes to the GND rail and its RIGHT contact goes through C1 to the amplifier input. I assumed the jack breakout has wires soldered on.
The tutorial lists '2 x 100k, 2 x 47k'. Resistor values were taken from the schematic labels: R8 and R9 are 100k, R10 and R11 are 47k. The image colour bands are not fully legible.
The second red wire and the black wire from the Arduino use GND.1 and IOREF. The Zero's GND pin choice is arbitrary; both GND pins are one net.
